recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the work group wants a historical narrative about the Feed-to-Bundle design transition, handle it as a new current editorial issue rather than as a late source edit for FHIR-5436.
issue_request: FHIR-5436 was a Published FHIR-core FHIR Infrastructure ballot comment for DSTU1 FHIR-core-Feed asking for a summary of why FHIR moved away from ATOM and what design improvements the new approach offered; the final Jira disposition was Considered - No action required and approved the currently published continuous build text.
initial_application: No exact FHIR-5436 source-changing commit was found. Jira records approval of the current build on 2015-02-12, and 2015 Bundle/Feed path history shows broad Bundle work before DSTU2 but no explicit application commit for this no-action issue.
additional_context: The current build actively scopes this area to Bundle: source/fhir.ini lists bundle=Bundle, assigns Bundle to the FHIR work group and infrastructure normative package, and has no Feed resource entry. Current Bundle definition and introduction source describe Bundle as a container/collection mechanism for resources, while current Bundle source contains no Atom wording. Community searches found no exact Confluence Jira reference or relevant Zulip/Confluence discussion changing the no-action interpretation.
reconciliation: No source changes were made. Adding a new ATOM migration rationale now would reopen an old editorial suggestion that was approved as no-action/currently published and is not necessary for current implementer-facing Bundle semantics.
